seo.title: Coral Guardian Partnership - Oceans Alive Foundation
seo.description: In partnership with the local nonprofit Coral Guardian, we collaborate on the REEL Kilifi project - Restoring Reef Ecosystems for Enhanced Livelihoods in Kenya.

hero.eyebrow: In Partnership with the Local Nonprofit
hero.title: Restoring Reefs,
hero.label: Rebuilding Lives
hero.text: Together with Coral Guardian, we're pioneering community-led coral restoration in the Kuruwitu Marine Protected Area - where conservation meets livelihoods.

theReelKilifiProject.heading: The REEL Kilifi
theReelKilifiProject.label: Project
theReelKilifiProject.boldText: Restoring Reef Ecosystems for Enhanced Livelihoods
theReelKilifiProject.text: is more than a coral restoration project - it's a transformative initiative in Kenya's Indian Ocean waters.
theReelKilifiProject.text2: The project unfolds in the 12,000-hectare Kuruwitu coastal co-management area in Kilifi County. This pioneering zone benefits from shared coastal and marine resource management between the government and the local fishing community, making it a beacon of effective collaborative conservation in Kenya.
theReelKilifiProject.text3: "A pioneer in effective collaborative conservation in Kenya - where communities and government protect the ocean together."

restorationTechniques.heading: Our Restoration
restorationTechniques.label: Techniques
restorationTechniques.text: Methods adapted and replicable by local communities, ensuring sustainable impact.
restorationTechniques.text2: We use methods that are adapted and replicable by local communities. On-site coral nurseries house fragments of opportunity corals collected in the area.
restorationTechniques.text3: Fishermen trained in coral biology and restoration methods over several months
restorationTechniques.text4: Restoration within the Tengefu law protected area, ensuring sustainability
restorationTechniques.text5: We're testing new methods to find the most appropriate and financially sustainable approaches for this unique environment.

communityInvolvement.heading: Involving Local
communityInvolvement.label: Communities
communityInvolvement.text: The community plays a central role in the adoption and implementation of the project - from training to teaching to shared ownership.
communityInvolvement.text2: To develop a sense of ownership in the local community by fostering peer-to-peer learning in the context of community citizen science, and by sharing the results of the project with the immediate and wider community.

monitoringAndEvaluation.heading: Monitoring &
monitoringAndEvaluation.label: Evaluation
monitoringAndEvaluation.text: We track both ecological and social outcomes to ensure lasting, meaningful impact.

lookingAhead.heading: Looking Ahead:
lookingAhead.label: Project Evolution
lookingAhead.subheading: From Local Success to Regional Model
lookingAhead.text: The overall aim of this collaboration is to strengthen and extend the participatory coral reef restoration models implemented in the Kuruwitu Tengefu Community Protection Area in Kenya, in order to support local communities.
lookingAhead.text2: The Kuruwitu area will serve as a living classroom for training new communities, sharing experiences and best practices across the region.
lookingAhead.text3: Following a restoration approach adapted to the socio-economic context of local traditional fishing communities - scalable and sustainable.
lookingAhead.text4: "This partnership represents more than coral restoration - it's about empowering communities to become the guardians of their own marine heritage, creating a model that can be replicated across Kenya's coast and beyond."

callToAction.heading: Support Community-Led
callToAction.label: Coral Restoration
callToAction.text: Your contribution directly funds training, equipment, and long-term monitoring for the REEL Kilifi project - empowering local communities to restore their reefs and secure their livelihoods.
